clue.text: Man, for instance, may be in the way

definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man is a piece of land surrounded by sea
a traffic refuge in the middle of a road stands in the path of vehicles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: an isle such as Man, and a raised refuge in a roadway that sits in traffic's path.

clue.text: Convict in poor shape, building a refuse dump

indicators.note: in places the convict inside the jumbled letters
poor suggests the word shape is badly formed and so rearranged

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner in bad condition is constructing a rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' is the anagram signal, not a description of the convict; 'in' sets LAG inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of mining waste or other spoil is a pile of rubbish.

clue.text: Army rising outside Paris about one who employs a lot of workers

definitions.text: one who employs a lot of workers

indicators.note: about says the whole assembly wraps around the letter for one
outside means the turned army letters go around the city's name
rising in a down clue means the army letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Soldiers climbing up round Paris around one boss with a big workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses TA in this down clue, 'outside' wraps that around Paris, and 'about' wraps the lot around I. The workers are worker bees.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper looks after worker bees by the thousand.

clue.text: Abandons ice cream container, making this in the kitchen

parts.note: drops means gives up or abandons
a cone is the wafer that holds ice cream

explanation.surface: Someone discards a wafer cone while baking.
explanation.walkthrough: A drop scone is a small thick pancake, made by dropping batter onto a griddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thick pancake cooked on a griddle is a homemade teatime dish.

clue.text: Naturally chosen to work in pool first, in college second

indicators.note: first says this piece starts the answer, before the college part

parts.note: typing is the work done in a typing pool of an office

indicators.note: in places the letter for second inside the college abbreviation

parts.note: CAT stood for a College of Advanced Technology in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone is picked to work first in a typing pool, then at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue had a stray apostrophe before 'work'; the page has none. 'in' puts S inside CAT, a College of Advanced Technology, a British institution of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor cast in a role that suits their natural manner or looks is picked to match a stock part.

clue.text: Fetch book by dean — uncommon in this out-of-the-way place

indicators.note: uncommon suggests the words are put into an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: Bringing a book by a churchman is rare in such a remote spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommon' rearranges the fifteen letters of FETCH BOOK BY DEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a remote, isolated place far from towns.

clue.text: An ingredient in water, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: one of the four classical substances alongside earth, air and fire

explanation.walkthrough: 'in water' tempts you toward hydrogen; the word instead names water itself as one of the ancient four.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a constituent part, and one of the four classical substances of ancient thought.

clue.text: A drink exalted in the Orient. What's your poison?

indicators.note: exalted, raised up, in a down clue means the drink is read upwards and so backwards

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A glass of something raised in the East, with an offer of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exalted' turns PORT to TROP, read upwards in this down clue. 'What's your poison?' is a jokey offer of a drink, here taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade.

clue.text: Speculator — one who believes gold is buried

indicators.note: is buried places the gold inside the word for a believer

parts.note: a theist believes in God
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A dealer who speculates believes that gold is hidden in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speculates by forming hypotheses rather than testing them.

clue.text: A singer found it in the beginning of a song

indicators.note: in places the little word it inside the phrase for the opening of a song

parts.note: music opens at bar one, the first bar of the score

explanation.surface: A vocalist discovers something at the start of a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the beginning of a song' is read as a musician would: the first bar, BAR ONE. 'in' places IT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice between tenor and bass, and so a kind of singer.

clue.text: Scholar's grade of crime?

parts.note: a university qualification awarded to a scholar, and the grading of an offence, as in first or second level murder

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves both the academic award and the legal grading of a crime such as murder.
explanation.definitionFit: A university award is a graduate's qualification, and murder is graded as first or second in US law.

clue.text: Tea is mother's spiritual power!

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic claim that a mother's cup of tea has a mystical force.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a divinely conferred gift or grace, now a compelling personal magnetism.

clue.text: Drink without exercise gives the alarm signal

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the drink goes around the exercise

parts.note: beer is a common drink
PE is physical education, exercise at school

explanation.surface: Drinking instead of working out sets off a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the drink wraps around the exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager or buzzer that emits a bleep to warn or summon is named by the signal it makes.

clue.text: Vessel takes river out of Greater Manchester area

indicators.note: out of says the letter for river is removed from the town's name

parts.note: Stockport is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A ship steams up a river away from a town near Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Stockport is a town near Manchester; 'out of' removes R from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cooking pot for simmering bones into broth is a kitchen vessel.

clue.text: In Sumatra he eats fruit mostly, a nut exceptionally

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the fruit is dropped

parts.note: an orange is a fruit

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests the words a nut are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: An ape in Sumatra mostly eats fruit, and a nut only rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves ORANG, and 'exceptionally' rearranges A NUT as UTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The great red ape lives only in the forests of Sumatra and Borneo.

clue.text: Small point of land causing endless ill will

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word for malice is cut off

parts.note: spite is malice or ill will

explanation.surface: A tiny headland is the cause of unending bad feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow tongue of sand or shingle running out into the sea is a small headland.

clue.text: Haphazard upbringing of unhappy friend in Scottish Borders

indicators.note: in places the turned pieces inside the edges of Scottish
the borders of a word are its first and last letters
upbringing, bringing up in a down clue, means the pieces are read upwards and so backwards

parts.note: sad means unhappy
pal means friend

explanation.surface: A careless childhood for a miserable companion in the region of Scotland bordering England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish Borders is a region of Scotland next to England. 'upbringing of' reverses the two pieces together in this down clue, giving LAPDAS, which 'in' puts inside S and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Done hastily and carelessly, in a random manner.

clue.text: Impressive announcement that one's portrait is being painted

definitions.text: announcement that one's portrait is being painted
definitions.meaning: what a sitter for an artist might say: I am sitting as a model

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: grand in appearance, and a sitter's declaration of modelling, split as two words.

clue.text: Break all the others

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a pause from activity, and the remainder of a group.

clue.text: Again clothe a partially-clad soldier

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, so a soldier
wearing only a vest, so in vest

explanation.surface: Dressing once more a soldier who is only half dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: To invest someone is to robe them, as at an investiture.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to robe someone in the insignia of office, so doing it again is dressing them anew.

clue.text: With which to wipe down Siegfried's first, strange horse? Not right

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the name
not right means the letter R, for right, is removed

parts.note: queer means strange
gee, or gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: Asking what to rub down Siegfried's odd horse with, since something is amiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' removes R from QUEER to leave QUEE; GEE-GEE is a child's word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber-bladed tool for wiping water off windows or floors.

clue.text: Risen unaided in same field, perhaps?

definitions.text: Risen unaided in same field, perhaps?

parts.words: Risen unaided in same field, perhaps?
parts.note: a person who rose without help, with same field nudging toward the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone climbed to the top of their profession on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: SAME FIELD has nine letters, one I more than the answer, so it is a nudge rather than a true anagram; the clue as a whole describes a person who succeeded alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes someone who achieved wealth or rank by their own efforts rather than through inheritance or help.

clue.text: A green revolution supported by a church

indicators.note: supported by in a down clue puts the first piece on top of what follows

parts.note: a spin is a turn or revolution

explanation.surface: An environmentalist uprising backed by a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like politics but is a leafy vegetable; 'supported by' sets SPIN above A and CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy vegetable is one of the greens on the plate.

clue.text: Entering mine because returns reveal pecuniary gain

indicators.note: entering places the turned word inside the word for mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: returns means the word for because is read backwards

parts.note: for can mean because

explanation.surface: Going into a mine since the takings show a financial gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses the word for because to give ROF, and 'Entering' puts that inside the mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Money made in excess of costs is a financial gain.

clue.text: Father is, in French, masculine for example

parts.note: en is French for in
masculine is one grammatical class of nouns, alongside feminine and neuter

explanation.surface: A father is described in French as being of the masculine sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to beget.
explanation.definitionFit: To beget or bring about something, as a parent produces offspring.

clue.text: Creature in a pound, chasing retreating bird

indicators.note: chasing puts the a and pound pieces behind the turned bird
retreating means the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: the mina, also spelt myna, is an Asian starling
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: An animal in a pen pursues a bird that is backing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' reverses the bird to ANIM; 'chasing' sets A and L after it. L for pound comes from Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living beast or creature is one of the fauna.

clue.text: Unacceptable habit, say, to take precedence

parts.note: out can mean not acceptable, as in quite out of the question

indicators.note: say signals that the word for habit is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: a way is a habit or custom

explanation.surface: A bad habit, so to speak, takes priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you WAY is spoken and then written as WEIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: To be more important or heavier than something else is to take priority over it.

clue.text: Selfishly appropriate explosive hidden in blue cask

parts.note: to hog is to keep greedily to oneself

indicators.note: hidden in places the explosive inside the word for blue

parts.note: blue means sad or low
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: Grabbing for oneself some dynamite concealed in a blue barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: HE for high explosive is a crossword staple; 'hidden in' is the container signal here, not a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: A large barrel, traditionally holding about 54 gallons of beer.

clue.text: Mace for the head girl

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A can of spray for the senior pupil at a girls' school.
explanation.walkthrough: A head girl is the senior pupil at a British school; here head is NUT and the girl is MEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is the spice made from the lacy outer coat of the same seed, so the two spices are closely linked.
